steps.speaker: Refugee Boy
steps.content: Thani, can we... can we rest for a bit? Dima can't walk anymore.
The children's voices pierced the silent night of WhiteSands. They'd left trails of tiny footprints in the sand. Beneath their refugee cloaks, their faces were all young yet weary.
The girl leading them stopped immediately, turned around, and gazed up at the pale moon hanging in the night sky.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: Then let's camp here for the night. Hmm, it's a bit exposed out here... but we should be fine! Shura, can you help me?
A frail figure darted out from the group. The girl looked barely older than ten. She pulled out various tools and supplies from her backpack and handed them to Thani.

The children sat in a circle with Thani standing in the center, skillfully building a fire and cooking. Shura produced a waterskin from her backpack and handed it to the companion beside her. The children each took just a small sip before passing it to the next person. The firelight illuminated their faces.

steps.speaker: Refugee Boy
steps.content: Hey, Dima, why aren't you drinking?

steps.speaker: Refugee Girl
steps.content: Thani... we've been running in WhiteSands for so long. Will we... ever get back to the refugee camp?

As soon as the girl spoke, the chattering children instantly fell silent, looking down and fidgeting with their fingers. For a moment, the only thing they could hear was Thani's spoon stirring and clinking against the pot.

steps.speaker: Refugee Girl
steps.content: Does that mean... I'll never see Mom and Dad again?

steps.speaker: Refugee Boy
steps.content: Dima, please don't...

steps.speaker: Refugee Girl
steps.content: If I'd known it would be like this, I should have just stayed with Mom and Dad...

steps.speaker: Refugee Boy
steps.content: Stay with them? They were long gone! Dead! Don't you get it? Is that what you want too, to die with them?!

steps.speaker: Refugee Boy
steps.content: ...Oh no, d-don't cry!

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: Who says everyone's gone?
Thani stopped what she was doing. The crying ceased instantly. The girl looked up, meeting Thani's smile.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: Don't believe what those DisCity people say!

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: Granny Afra once told me that we children of WhiteSands are blessed by the Desert Goddess. Even when we die, our souls become sand and we live on forever, always staying with our families.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: Everyone's been away from home for so long that they've forgotten this truth. No matter how cruelly the DisCity people treat us, they can never truly separate us. We've fooled them all!
Thani's vehemence grew with every word, and she thrust her arm upward, slicing it through the air with a fierce gesture.

steps.speaker: Refugee Boy
steps.content: Thani... that sounds like... something Granny made up to comfort you...

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: Hehe, I used to think the same thing. But you know what? I can still hear Granny's favorite song in the wind sometimes.

steps.speaker: Refugee Girl
steps.content: Thani, can you really hear it?

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: Of course! Don't you trust my ears?

steps.speaker: Refugee Girl
steps.content: Then... can you try to see if you can catch any messages Mom and Dad left for me?

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: Sure thing! Let's see...
Thani closed her eyes, cupping one hand to her ear while gently resting the other on the girl's shoulder, as if to soothe her anxiety.

The night was still, yet she heard the children's hopeful breaths, barely suppressed. In the distance, a lone beast growled at the moon. Blown by the wind, the sand rippled like waves, spreading across the darkness.
Suddenly, her brow furrowed slightly. Her eyes remained closed, but her body froze for an instant as if catching some signal, her breath momentarily caught.
She could hear it now. Footsteps were approaching across the undulating sand, faint yet distinct.
Thani opened her eyes, the smile still on her face.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: I heard them! Your mom and dad are warning us about approaching danger. We need to pack up quickly now, but don't worry. They'll help hold back those bad guys for a while!

steps.speaker: Shura
steps.content: Thani? Could it be... those people from the institute again?!

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: Shh... pack up your things quickly now. Shura, lead everyone back the way we came. Remember, don't make any noise.
Thani raised an index finger to her lips in a shushing gesture. Her eyes, however, already turned toward the distance, as if she'd spotted something.

steps.speaker: Shura
steps.content: Thani, aren't you coming with us? In that case... I'm staying too!

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: I can't let them go alone. Remember those trail markers we've been using? I'll follow them to catch up with you all.

steps.speaker: Shura
steps.content: B-but if you don't come with us, everyone will be terrified! What if... what if!
Shura looked away. Thani watched her, a rare shadow shrouding her eyes for just a moment. But her smile quickly returned, just as it always did.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: Trust me, I won't be like those adults... I promise I'll catch up with you in three days. Three days, tops!
Shura looked up at that familiar smile, the one that always made even the worst disasters feel tolerable, and finally nodded decisively.

steps.speaker: Shura
steps.content: Leave it to me then! I promise I won't lose a single one of them before you come back!
Thani bent down and stoked the fire higher, the smoke providing cover as the children hastily packed up and helped one another disappear into the distance.
Now, with her companions gone and the desert beasts asleep, Thani turned around. What she faced was nothing but waves of black sand, surging toward her in relentless torrents.
The waves were getting closer, growing larger.
Sandy wind whipped her face, slicing her cheeks. Thani flinched from the stinging pain, but quickly steadied herself, planting her feet firmly into the sand.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: Now, I'll need the blessings from all of you back at the refugee camp...

She murmured to herself, lifting her hand to touch the metal bracelet on her wrist. In the next moment, her fingers clenched tightly around her wooden staff as she swept it across the ground, kicking up clouds of sand.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: Hey! You! I'm right here! Come and get me!
[Empty Shot]

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: This is the Outlander girl our patrol rescued from WhiteSands.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Did you capture her attackers?

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: No. Though they were outnumbered, the attackers knew WhiteSands better than we did and were clearly well-trained. Once they realized they were losing, they retreated without a second thought. We've conducted a few searches since then, but so far there's been no sign of them.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: However, we have managed to gather some information about the victim's identity.
Nightingale turns her head, and you follow her gaze toward the interrogation room. The girl sits in a chair, occasionally glancing at you both through the glass.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Her name is Thani. An A-Class Sinner with severe Mania corruption. On top of that, she has been exposed to Aurum Secretum radiation.

The medical report in your hand reads: Severe Mania resulting from Aurum Secretum infection. The subject exhibits hypersensitivity for all five senses. Under high-stress situations, she may also experience symptoms such as fainting and shock.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Aurum Secretum... What's her connection to Fraser?

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Given that our patrol found her near the Aurum Secretum Research Institute, we suspect she may have direct ties to the facility, or possibly even to BR-005, but...
Nightingale shakes her head.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: We currently have no concrete evidence linking them. She was recently attacked and is still in shock, which explains her guarded attitude toward us.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: But I believe you can gain her trust.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I see. Open the door for me, please.
The interrogation room's seat is hard and cold. Though Thani has tucked the hem of her jacket beneath her to avoid direct contact of her skin with the metal, she can't stop fidgeting uncomfortably.
She unconsciously touches her wrist, which is now completely bare.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: We're keeping your bracelet for now. It helps manage your Aurum Secretum symptoms, doesn't it? It's taken quite a bit of wear and tear though. We'll return it to you once it's repaired.
Thani remains silent. You give her a gentle smile.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: This is the Minos Bureau of Crisis Control, an organization that shelters and rehabilitates Sinners. I'm the Chief here. The people who rescued you from your attackers and brought you here are also our staff.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: Th-thank you all...

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: What about those bad guys? Did you catch them all?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I'm afraid we didn't catch any of them. We only managed to save you.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: Oh, really...

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: Then did you see anyone else? Besides the attackers?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: There were others?

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: No! I, I was just... wondering! I just think I got really lucky... Hehe, I'm the sole survivor, aren't I...
She says this, but her hands can't stop fussing with the hem of her clothes.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Just wondering?
Thani glances at you, then quickly averts her eyes.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I understand you're frightened. You were attacked and woke up in a strange place. But please trust me. We mean you no harm. We only want to help you.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: If you know who attacked you, or have any other relevant information, please tell me. Including anything about these others you mentioned.

She opens her mouth, about to say something, when the overhead light suddenly flickers. She flinches, shielding her eyes with her hand. When she regains her composure, she glances around the room with newfound suspicion, presses her lips together, and decides to remain silent.
She can't bring herself to trust you in this setting. You decide to change tactics and try to find another way past her defenses.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: When our team rescued you, you had no food supplies or tools, not even a water bottle. Without these essentials, no one could survive more than three days in the desert.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Unless you weren't the one carrying these necessities.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: I did have supplies with me! I was carrying several kilos of dried food. But... but...

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: The desert bandits took everything! That's right! Those thieves are ruthless. They stole all my food and water, even took my can opener...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You said you had several kilos of dried food. Was that all just for you?

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: Huh? Y-yes. How else would it be enough for... I mean, enough for me...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You were lugging several kilos of food, plus water and tools, on your own, trekking through WhiteSands for months? You must be some kind of miracle.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: Don't judge me by my size! I'm actually super strong! Back at the refugee camp, I even helped build houses...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Which refugee camp?
You cut her off abruptly, giving her no time to think. Thani freezes, her face visibly turning red.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: Geez, whichever you think it is! Just some random refugee camp! Why do you have to dig into everything...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: So why did you leave the refugee camp? Sure, it might not be the most comfortable home, but it must be better than wandering alone?

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: I just wanted to! There's no why... The folks there... the folks at the camp bullied me! No, wait... it was because of the desert bandits! Hmm... no, there was a sandstorm! I left because...
You interrupt her again.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Or, was the refugee camp destroyed?

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: ...What?
She falls silent, staring at you in shock. You move closer, looking directly into her eyes.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: The place where we found you isn't far from the bombed Aurum Secretum Research Institute.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: From what I know, there used to be a refugee camp near the institute. Now, like the facility itself, it's been completely burned to the ground.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You claim you're from the refugee camp and that you're being hunted by unknown pursuers. At the same time, you're also infected with Aurum Secretum.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I'll stop going around in circles. Tell me, what is your connection to the Aurum Secretum Research Institute?
Thani snaps back to reality, her eyes darting frantically around the room. Finally, with a defiant tilt of her chin, she says:

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: ...Okay, okay! You're right, I'm from there. But I'm no refugee, I'm...
Thani unconsciously yanks at her tattered sleeve.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: I'm a researcher from the Fraser Institute! So you'd better let me go right now, or else... or else...
Seeing your unfazed expression, her voice gradually dwindles.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: Or else... something bad will happen...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Even if you really were from the Fraser Institute, we still couldn't just let you go. Your life would be in constant danger out there. And not just because someone's hunting you down.
You sigh and pick up a document from the desk.
test
test
test
test
test
test

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Our doctors have examined you. You're suffering from severe Mania infection. Without immediate suppression treatment, you'll soon lose your mind completely and turn into a Corruptor.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: How is that possible...? My mind is perfectly clear right now, except for a few minor side effects...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: The corruption in your body has progressed thoroughly. Those Aurum Secretum marks on your skin are proof. You may feel relatively normal now, but once your Mania flares up, you'll deteriorate much faster than others.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Thani, you don't have much time left.
Thani's body begins to tremble. You soften your voice to comfort the shivering girl before you.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: But don't be afraid. I have a way to help you.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: R-Really?!

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Yes, this is part of my job. But first, I need to know what really happened to you and why you were wandering in WhiteSands.
Thani's eyes dart nervously as her lips tremble. You notice her defenses weakening and adjust your tone accordingly.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I know you don't trust me. When you asked if I'd seen anyone else, you were checking whether your companions were safe, weren't you?

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: I... I was just afraid you might have killed them...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: On the contrary, we want to protect all of you.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: Why should I believe you? The people at Fraser said the same thing before, and then...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Because we're investigating the incident related to the Aurum Secretum Research Institute. And by that I mean we're seeking the truth, not silencing witnesses. If you and your companions are connected to the facility, then ensuring your safety is our absolute priority.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Furthermore, as I mentioned, I'm Chief of this Bureau that shelters Sinners, which means your safety matters to me.
Your voice softly fades away, followed by a long silence. Thani hangs her head as tears fall silently onto her knees.
Finally, she tilts up her face, wiping away the dampness with her hand, a glimmer of tears still lingering in her eyes.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: I did grow up in the refugee camp outside the Aurum Secretum Research Institute. Until that massive explosion happened. I remember that day, when the entire sky went dark.
Without a doubt, that massive explosion Thani refers to is BR-005.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: What happened before and after the explosion?

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: We found out the Aurum Secretum Research Institute was experimenting on refugees, turning them into monsters. So we helped blow the place up.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: But after it was all over, suddenly, the adults said they needed to attend a sacrificial ritual... They followed Saffar, and then... the explosion happened, and they all turned into monsters just like the Apostles.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: ...They died.
Thani's voice gradually fades until it's barely audible.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: Before they left, they told me to take care of the other kids and stay alive. I originally planned for us to keep living at the refugee camp. But after that, the institute came for us and burned everything down. I overheard them saying that they had to eliminate all evidence.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: So I took everyone and left. I thought maybe we could find somewhere to stay in WhiteSands.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: So you are the evidence. Living, breathing witnesses who know what happened.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: I don't know anything about what happened inside... I just... wanted us all to survive together.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Where are your companions now?

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: Still in WhiteSands. I promised them I'd go back. They left markers that we used to leave when playing games. Only we know about them.
Thani bites her lip, her shoulders trembling slightly.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: They're still waiting for me to come back. I promised them...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I'll help you bring them back. Tell us about these markers so we know where to find them.
You stand up, retrieve a piece of paper and a pen from the desk, and hand them to her.
She hesitates for a moment before taking the pen with a tremulous hand. But just as she's about to write, her hand suddenly stops. She looks up at you.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: ...You said I'm very sick. If I actually die from this illness, will you still look for them?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Yes. Your health condition is a separate matter from their rescue mission.
You give her a smile.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Besides, we won't let it come to that.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: All right...
She lowers her head and slowly begins drawing symbols on the paper. But her hand shakes, making her drawing slow and messy. When she finishes, she looks up again.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: So... when you find them, will I be able to stay with them?
You pause for a moment, not answering her directly.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: This is a facility reserved for Sinners. So, if none of your companions show signs of Mania like you do, we'll place them in an orphanage where they'll be taken care of and receive education.
Thani's shoulders slowly slump with each word you speak.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: So... I'll be separated from everyone? Even if... even if I recover?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: It won't be a goodbye. You'll get to visit them, I promise.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: No. Then I don't want to be treated anymore. You all claim you're helping me, but you're just tearing us apart!
She tries to stand up abruptly, but something seems to scratch against her skin. She instantly curls up with a sharp hiss of pain, pressing hard against the spot where her bracelet once was.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You want to protect them, don't you? You've done everything possible to help them escape from the refugee camp and evade the pursuers... If you want to keep them safe, you should start by getting yourself treated, so they won't have to worry about you.
You approach slowly, squatting down to meet her at eye level.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I can help you. I'll place my shackles on you, which can control your Mania and alleviate your Aurum Secretum symptoms.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Please trust me.
She grits her teeth wordlessly, her eyes filled with conflicted emotions. After a long moment, she finally speaks in a small voice.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: ...What exactly are these shackles?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Put simply, it's a link between a Sinner and myself.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: A link... So, once I have these shackles on me, you'll be able to find me whenever you want?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Technically speaking, yes, that is part of its function. In your current situation, it would also allow me to check on your safety at any time.
Thani purses her lips.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: Can I... have some time to think about it...?
Under the harsh lights of the interrogation room, Thani's face is deathly pale, sweat pouring down her skin, yet her eyes remain defiant. After a long moment, you finally nod.

That night, you dispatch operatives to WhiteSands. You suspect Thani wants to see her companions one last time before accepting the shackles, but her infection is already too bad. Meanwhile, Fraser's assassins are closing in on the children. Time is running out for everyone.
<i>But the next day, Thani is gone.
